lines.st: Today a ship sets sail♪
Past the lighthouse, past the church♪
The damp sea mist drifts to the shore♪
"Raise the sails"—the helm's not in the wind's hands♪
Today a ship sets sail♪
A sailor's love never weeps when we part♪
She knows I'll bring back pearls and gold♪
And wine and sugar without end♪
Today a ship sets sail♪
A fowlbeast paces on the rail—♪
Let it wait in vain. Sound the horn, haul in the nets♪
We haul up the sun♪

lines.x: Today a ship sets sail♪
She bears no name, only a captain young and brave♪
He can—♪
Uh, he can...
He can point the way through the raging gale♪
Call him Iberia—every shore he reaches is home♪
Ugh, I can never get this line down. Valerio, how many times have you had to remind me now?
Six times, Tefi.
It's not your fault. This shanty's been banned in Iberia for over sixty years—it's not easy to learn again. Your pronunciation's gotten much better than before.
"Much better" isn't good enough. Once upon a time, everyone from the fin-fishers in the remote villages of the south to the captains of the Iberian Royal Navy fleet hummed this melody.
When fleets of golden ships set sail from our Port City—Rea-Iberia—the singing of the crowds shook the very reefs along the shore.
A pity the Profound Silence took it all away sixty-three years ago...

Dozens of cities, the Port City first among them, sank one after another. Most things from the Golden Age, going to sea included, became taboo. Apart from farming and reciting scripture, people didn't dare dream of anything.
But the place we're going now isn't like anywhere else in Iberia.

It's the symbol of the Golden Age and the seafaring spirit. It's the place I've longed for most ever since I put on this naval uniform, and it's the perfect place to sing the shanty I've been practicing—
Provided we can get in. The Inquisition started vetting who could become a resident of the district three months ago. We don't qualify to move there.
The travel money you swindled... I mean, raised from your supporters is all spent. All we have left is this case in my hand.
Mm, it's about time. Quick, hand me the instrument from the case!

About time for what...
Hm? Is that a marching band?
(Cheerful music)
The sea shelters Iberia, my friend!
Th-the sea shelters? I've only ever heard my grandmother say that...
Isn't it the sea's shelter that's bringing Rea-Iberia back after sixty-three years under? Besides, today's the day the salvage operation for the Port City's Central District officially begins!
Of course! We've been marching all the way from the north. We're heading to the square in the Outer District to play for the ceremony.
You're just who I've been waiting for!
Huh?
I mean—your "The Old Sailor of Iberia" has been waiting for a trumpeter like me!
You've got a good ear, I'll give you that. That tune's a lot older than you are. Come on, join us. Today's going to be an extraordinary day for Iberia!
That's right!
Valerio, just blend in with the procession and you'll get into the Port City's Outer District, no problem.
Oh, I know you don't like it when I pull these little tricks, and I know you worry about me. It'll be fine.
Tefi...
Ah-ah-ah! Once we're in the Outer District, you can't call me by my real name. If we slip up, I won't be able to fool any supporters, and we won't make any money!
Remember, right now I'm not little Tefi who drifts from one fin-fishing village to the next—
My title is lost noble, scion of the Iberian Royal Navy—Estefanía Colón de Toledo!
Please present your identification and entry documents.
Go ahead.
Hello, please open the case.
Mm, everything's in order.
Ma'am, over there—weapons can't be carried in the streets during the ceremony. You...
Head up. With a performance like that, the only way you'll earn any merit doing basic patrol work is if every suspect sews their crimes onto their waistband.
Quick, tell me you're not actually dreaming that dream, Nando?
Instructor Drusa, I was just so focused that I didn't recognize you...
Focused? On patrolling, or on counting?
You stop the last of every five people who pass. A stupidly predictable pattern. If I were a criminal, the square would've blown sky-high already.
Please don't mock me. Doesn't patrol unit work have to follow Inquisition rules?
Strictly speaking, the only Ægir who's joined the Inquisition is that clerk who went home on leave. I'm a free agent, not on the books.
Even so, not everyone can ignore procedure like you and still be an instructor for so many years...
What did you say?
*cough*...
Hey! Wait, the girl in that marching band—I don't think I saw you on the registration list. Please present your identification.
Wh-what about me? Don't you like the trumpet, sir? The marching band can't be late—we're playing at the grand launch ceremony!
Shifty eyes, overexcited, and the way you're holding that trumpet—
Sigh, fine, fine, let her go.
Thank you, officer!
Instructor Drusa!
Look behind you. That band she's leading has blocked the whole street to the square, and more and more spectators are showing up. How do you plan to deal with that?
Checking them would only take ten-odd minutes. Before, we—
Stand down, soldier.
Tell me, where are we standing right now?
Where are we standing? We're standing in the Port City's Outer District.

A few months ago, under the plan of the Ægir Consul who partnered with us, it was salvaged ahead of the rest and fitted with a lighthouse power supply system and the giant cranes for raising the Central District.
Today's salvage launch ceremony is also a test of the power supply system and the salvage technology. The workers are going to raise the grandest statue of the king from the flooded Central District.
In two weeks, the Central District itself will be raised too. Then the place we're standing will become the true, complete Rea-Iberia.
Good answer, but what you're describing is a change in administrative divisions. What I want to point out is how this district differs from the rest of Iberia.
How it differs?
A lot of the facilities and workplaces here are built right on the sea. People can't quite look at the ocean admiringly yet, but they're not afraid to live by the water anymore.
The lighthouses, the Salvage Center, the shipyard... You see Islanders everywhere, and the Penal Battalion and the Inquisitors don't get to interrogate them on a whim anymore.
Churchgoers haven't gotten any fewer, but instead of confessing, more and more of them are sharing their visions of the future—their visions of Rea-Iberia, the capital of the Golden Age.
A month ago, everything to do with the Golden Age and the sea was still a sin engraved in scripture. Now, none of that is in the scripture as Su Santidad has reinterpreted it.
What does that tell you?
I've heard all of that, but I've also heard people start questioning Su Santidad's judgment because of it. I can't voice an opinion rashly.

But I understand what you mean, Instructor. We really are standing at a crossroads of change for Iberia. It's just that when I joined the Inquisition, I swore an oath. I have to stand firm at my post.

Sigh, all right, enough. There are several Inquisitors in the square, and hundreds of Penal Battalion soldiers with more experience than you. They're not there for show. If they think you're overstepping, you'll be in trouble.
Besides, even if you don't trust them, surely you trust the two officials who matter most to all of Iberia right now?
Saint Carmen, the last Saint, and Ms. Clementia, who proposed the Salvage Plan... They're already at the ceremony?
No one cares more about the salvage operation that's about to begin, or about this ceremony, than they do. Relax.
Aged seaweed liquor—who wants some aged seaweed liquor—
Aged seaweed liquor?
You wouldn't know this, but it's a brewing craft passed down through my family for generations. It saw my ancestors through the hardest days after the Profound Silence. It means a lot.
On a day like today, you're not brewing anything new?
Sigh, I'll be honest with you. I brought all this liquor from my hometown after I got approved to move here. I was afraid this place would be even worse than the rundown town I used to live in.
Who knew it'd turn out to be such a good place? So good I almost thought I'd stepped outside Iberia's borders... *ahem*, I shouldn't say things like that.
I'd like to brew new liquor too, but someone's got to drink the old stuff, right?
You're right. I'll have a glass.

Thank you.
Hm, judging by your clothes, you don't look like an Islander—more like one of the Ægir from the sea...
Wait, are you the Ægir Consul who proposed the Salvage Plan?
Haha, the way you put it, Islanders and "Ægir from the sea" like me sound like two completely different kinds of people.
Th-that's... That's not what I meant, Your Excellency!
Hm, I thought I was just making a joke? It seems Iberia and Ægir don't find the same things funny...
Language module, record conversational context, analyze discrepancy—my apologies, friend. I've studied Iberian, but I'm still not entirely fluent.
I-it's fine.
Sigh...
You really are different from those Hunter companions of yours.
The mission they shoulder is far heavier than the responsibilities I carry.
If they had the chance to live in Iberia instead of carrying out missions to exterminate the Seaborn, I don't think they'd be quite so intimidating either.
Though if that were the case, the joint land-sea defense line we built wouldn't have been enough for us to go ahead with the Salvage Plan, Lord Iberia.
Late one night a few months ago, an Ægir drone appeared outside the window of Inquisition headquarters and lit up the mark I had made on an old sea chart—Rea-Iberia.
I think that coincidence simply shows we had already reached an agreement before negotiations began.
Just as the last time Iberians and Ægir worked hand in hand to build this amphibious city beneath our feet.
And my attitude toward the Ægir will be no different from what it was then.
You still have doubts about Ægir's true purpose in helping Iberia salvage the Port City, don't you?
"Giving a people confined to the land a port to the world once more" is nothing but a stale and quietly dangerous piece of diplomatic rhetoric.
Whether you are the exception, or simply too invested in this cooperation—I know full well that Ægir does not yet care for its kin scattered across the land, let alone for the nation of Iberia...
Consul Clementia, I remember your record. Before you became Consul of Milliarium, you served as an Exercitus Commander.
Yes.
Then tell me—are you still a soldier unconditionally loyal to Ægir?
For the next two weeks, I'll be nothing more than the Salvage Center's new Supervisor, nothing more than kin to the Islanders.
The Port City's return doesn't just matter to the people of Iberia—it matters just as much to my kin. Or rather, that's really why you approved the Salvage Plan so quickly.
Hm?
I'd imagine you wouldn't cancel a Salvage Plan that took so long to prepare over a few words from me.
The Profound Silence was a devastating blow to Iberia. The Inquisition has made many efforts to ensure Iberia's survival—some admirable, others harsh, even bloody.
Now Rea-Iberia is about to return, and the Outer District's administration has been completely overhauled. Iberia will stand up again in the fierce sea wind, but many problems remain.
Scripture can be reinterpreted, but it can't be overturned entirely. To rid Iberians of their fear of the ocean, you first need to rid them of their deep-rooted fear of the Islanders.
Still, even with the Inquisition relaxing its restrictions on Islanders, and even with Rea-Iberia being a city with entirely new rules, this problem remains a thorny one for the Inquisition.
But if someone were to put a little diplomatic "pressure" on the Inquisition, the conflict between Iberians and Islanders wouldn't flare up again for the time being. For instance—
Deliberately having Ægir intervene in the Islander question.

You and I both know that to the vast majority of Ægir, none of what you've described even qualifies as a diplomatic dilemma. Nominally, you came to Iberia for one reason only—to carry out the Salvage Plan.
Yes, Lord Iberia. However...
Mm, Iberian seaweed liquor really doesn't taste any different from Ægir's. Before new liquor is brewed, someone has to drink the old.
To a fruitful partnership.
Sigh, what a mess. Who'd have thought so many Iberians would crowd the seaside? The band's been scattered by the crush.
The ceremony's about to start, and our trumpeter... How did she end up all the way at the front?!
My apologies, sir. She never listens...
Make way, make way! Please let the band's trumpeter—oh no, the conductor—stand at the very front to view the statue, so I can have enough passion and inspiration!
(Whispering) Memorize every detail of the statue and work out how to make the story hold together.
(Whispering) You're de Toledo, scion of the Royal Navy, here to rebuild the Royal Navy fleet, and you need plenty of funding—
Ow, stop shoving me!
Seaweed liquor—aged seaweed liquor—
(Whispering) What if nobody can cough up the money? Maybe life here isn't that easy either?
(Whispering) Then do it the old way. As long as Valerio and I get food and a bed, that's fine. Lady de Toledo is far more merciful than the Inquisition!
(Whispering) Does that line even work on anyone here anymore? I just saw two Penal Battalion soldiers laughing—scarier than when they interrogate people...
Hey, I said stop shoving! I'm—
Why'd it suddenly go quiet? What's everyone... looking up at?
The statue, with its timeworn sheen, blotted out the sun, its outline faintly aglow.
The sea roared as the statue rose, like great waves crashing on reefs, like wooden ships sinking into the fjord.
Tefi had traveled to many places in Iberia. What she heard today was no different from anything she'd heard before.
So why is my heart leaping like this? she wondered, dazed.
Three months ago, when she first heard the name "Rea-Iberia" from Valerio, all that came to mind were the stories the vagrants told.
Even as she posed as a noble, holding forth on the Golden Age to swindle meals and lodging, deep down she still thought the Port City was just a waterlogged ruin of a city, nothing special.
Now she stood among thousands of Iberians, raising her head with them, watching the king's statue hang over the land he had abandoned.
She seemed to see the sea.
The young Fernando Alejandro I stood on deck, squinting, aiming a sextant built on Ægir technology at the sun.
She seemed to hear singing.
A century ago, craftsmen made a statue of the king on deck, but the modeling took so long that the king's thoughts drifted far away. He hummed a shanty every Iberian knew by heart.
And so she, too, began to hum that lost shanty she had practiced countless times—
Today a ship sets sail♪
Past the lighthouse, past the church...♪
Hey, why's everyone just standing there? Where are the snare drums, the cornets? A hundred-year-old statue deserves a hundred-year-old song! Band, follow my lead!
The Liberi girl's singing rang out together with the band.
The elderly hummed along without thinking. Sixty-odd years had made them forget most of the lyrics, and the melody came out in fragments.
Young people with no instruments stomped their feet. The stationed Penal Battalion soldiers struck the stone steps with their weapons, the beat drowning out the distant waves.
People were still learning the unfamiliar shanty, still getting used to singing in broad daylight, but a feeling that had sunk with the Port City for so many years welled up in their hearts—
Today a ship sets sail♪
A fowlbeast paces on the rail—♪
Let it wait in vain. Sound the horn, haul in the nets♪
We haul up the sun♪
Finless ones, sixty-odd years still haven't purged you of your ignorance and arrogance...
Trying to take back the gift offered to the sea god—damn you, damn you...
That Ægir patrolling over there—I don't want to call her kin.
Soon you won't have to. Let her die of thirst on this barren land. Are you ready?
Mm.
Wait, your voice...
Urgh!
Church of the Deep activity has been dwindling lately, and you dare make trouble without any accomplices to help you?
Take them away.
Yes, sir.
Sir, it's a good thing you got that lead out of the Islanders locked in the dungeon. That's what stopped their scheme.
This may not end so easily.
Are you sure you don't need me and the other Penal Battalion soldiers to help you?
Your wounds still haven't healed. You should be resting more...
I didn't bring you all to the Port City's Outer District because I wanted a squad of soldiers loyal to me. I wanted to get you away from the battlefield, and away from interrogation work.
Su Santidad has reinterpreted scripture and relaxed restrictions on the Islanders living in the Outer District. That's a clear signal.

Even though we haven't yet won the war against the Seaborn, Iberia will soon usher in a brand-new era—we'll live in harmony with the Islanders. We won't need to hate each other, or turn our blades on one another.
Go have a glass of seaweed liquor in the square. Sing a song and dance with your friends and family.
Then... what do we do with these heretics?
I'll interrogate them.
The suspicious figures you spotted were indeed Church of the Deep cultists intent on sabotaging the ceremony.
Then can I take part in the interrogation?
What happens next isn't the patrol unit's concern. We'll handle it.
Why should—
Instructor Drusa, please keep an eye on this soldier. He just needs to finish his patrol duties. No rash moves.
Understood, understood.
"Rash moves"? I'm from the same intake as the soldiers who just hauled them off. We had exactly the same training!
I know. The first time you saw a Sea Terror, you screamed one less time than he did.
Instructor Drusa, you've taught at the Inquisition training grounds for ten years. Most of the new recruits in the Penal Battalion right now are your students.
And yet now you've been put in the same unit as me, doing the most basic patrol work. Doesn't it make you feel...
What's wrong with patrolling? Is arresting your own kin supposed to be a pleasure?
That's not what I meant...
Almost forgot. You, the technician in the water—you can lift your head now. The Penal Battalion's gone.
*gasp*... *gasp*...
Sorry about that. I was in a bit of a rush when I shoved you underwater. Your hand's not hurt, is it?
The hand you were holding down is a prosthetic anyway. I didn't feel a thing.
Good, good—no, I mean, that's a real shame...
Thank you for earlier, officer. If there's nothing else you need to ask, I'll go take care of the wrap-up on the statue salvage.
You were that rough with him and he's thanking you?
An Islander near the scene of a Church of the Deep arrest would definitely get questioned, even if he's a technician from the Salvage Center.
But you said it yourself—the Inquisition does things very differently in the Port City's Outer District. In interrogations... um... the less reasonable parts get avoided.
And how are they supposed to be sure they'll get a "proper" interrogation? Go down to the dungeon and find out firsthand?
That's...
I was watching what was happening underwater the whole time. He didn't take part in any of the cultists' actions.
Someone in my position isn't fit to vouch for an Islander, so all I could do was save him some trouble, in case this became the straw that broke his back. I've seen plenty of cases like that.
But just a few hours ago you were saying Rea-Iberia is different...
Yeah.
But right now, this half-finished district isn't the real Rea-Iberia yet, is it?
As a technician at the Salvage Center, he had rehearsed it carefully.

After finishing the statue salvage for the launch ceremony, he would leave through the water entrance on the north side of the square. That way he could avoid the busy main road, avoid trouble, and get back to the Salvage Center as quickly as possible.
Thanks to that officer. He didn't know how someone like her had joined the Inquisition, but life there probably wasn't any easier than it was for an ordinary Islander.

He wrung out his hair and clothes, threw on a waterproof coat, changed into land boots, and clenched his right hand three times to make sure the circuits in his prosthetic hadn't been affected by the seawater.
Corrosion spread outward from the prosthetic's joints, sending dull pain through him. With no medicine or toolbox on hand, he fended off the pain with willpower alone.
He needed treatment, but not today.
The weather balloon hasn't raised an alarm. Hovering steady...
A few hiccups along the way, but Grandma, just like you'd say, today's a good day for work.
The sea breeze still feels a little cold. I'll get used to it.
Hear the hammers and the saws, everyone? How long has it been since you saw a shipyard in Iberia?
Ship repair, sailmaking, reading the winds, drawing sea charts... Even if you've got no experience, you can learn from scratch.

Islanders needn't worry either! The Salvage Center and the shipyard are open to everyone equally. Everyone has a chance to help with the salvage of the Port City's Central District two weeks from now!
The Port City... the capital of the Golden Age... Scripture condemns it as one of the wellsprings of sin.
And the Islanders can't be trusted either. They're descendants of the ones who brought on the Profound Silence. They're an ill omen...
Stop repeating what the priests preach, Salvador. In two months on the road, it hasn't gotten us a single decent meal—but work at the shipyard can.
If that's so, why are so many people standing back and watching, just like us?
Bah, we all come from out-of-the-way fin-fishing villages. When have any of us seen anything like this?
There are Islanders all over the district, yet the Penal Battalion hardly ever questions them. When people greet each other, they don't quote scripture—they just ask if you've eaten your fill.
Honestly, I don't know what salvaging the Port City really means for us either, but if life is better here, I'm willing to go against a few teachings of scripture for a while.
Saints above, what would he think if he saw such chaos? We'd end up repenting in the Inquisition's dungeon...
I don't know what Su Santidad would think, but I do know that here, at least, the Inquisition isn't as harsh as it used to be.
...What proves it?
Look over there—even that little girl with her arm around the Golden Age statue hasn't been dragged off to the dungeon. What have we got to be afraid of?
*Ahem*. At the launch ceremony, before the eyes of the multitudes, it was this very shanty—conducted by me, led by my voice—that witnessed the king's statue being raised ashore.
Are you not curious how an unknown young woman could sing Iberia's century-old shanties? How she came to wear a naval uniform that doesn't fit her at all?
And how she could have the nerve to stand up to the Inquisition's own hiring office and give a speech, bold as brass, in the very square where the launch ceremony was just held?
Oh, some of you might say that ever since Saint Carmen announced the plan to salvage the Port City to all of Iberia, the doctrine the Inquisition upholds isn't what it used to be.
You poor things. I see several of you nodding, or looking lost... But their tolerance is clearly not the reason for my "audacity."
Now, do you see the gentleman beside me? Does anyone know his name?
This gentleman, once an admiral of the Iberian Royal Navy, Esteban Enríquez de Toledo—he and I are very closely connected...
Ah, you must have guessed already. After all, we look so alike, in dress and in feature!
The bone structure, the shape of the face, the placement of the ear feathers, even the texture of the hair... And this Royal Navy uniform I'm wearing—it's all evidence he left me!
In two weeks, Rea-Iberia will return. Aren't you curious whose hands that former royal capital will fall into?
Careful, the Inquisition's looking this way...
Don't worry. The de Toledo family appreciates everything the Inquisition has done for Iberia. I only wish to reclaim my family's legacy and treasures buried in the Port City's Central District.
Follow me, Estefanía Colón de Toledo, heir to the Iberian Royal Navy. With just a small donation...
Ah, I mean—so long as you support me, I will shelter you in turn, whatever your birth!
During the check the day before yesterday she said she was a trumpeter in a band. Now she's heir to the Iberian Royal Navy? And people are actually listening to such an obvious lie?
(Yawns) No moving in.
I know the Inquisition's being cautious about how it operates right now, but don't you think this "de Toledo" is really suspicious?
If my observations are right, there's definitely something off about her identity. She might not even have residency approval.
She went to all that trouble to sneak in. What if she means to sabotage the salvage operation... Instructor Drusa, I request permission to arrest her!
Denied.
I—
Don't rely too much on gut instinct, Nando.
I know, you want me to find evidence...
From the moment you start suspecting something, even if you don't have evidence, the first thing to do is look for patterns.
Patterns?
That's right. For example, a month ago, after the Salvage Center was finished, there were more than ten acts of sabotage in the city like the one the day before yesterday.
They don't seem connected at all. But if you're bored on checkpoint duty and you doodle on the Salvage Center's technician sign-in logs, you'll find some unexpected clues.
D-doodle?
That's not the point. The point is that while the technician we ran into the day before yesterday had nothing to do with the sabotage, there are a few particular technicians...
The days they worked underwater line up exactly with the days the sabotage happened.
Maybe that also explains why the Church of the Deep's been committing fewer crimes lately. It's not that they don't have help—it's that their helpers have changed.
You suspect the sabotage is connected to the Islanders at the Salvage Center? Then...
We're just patrol unit members. Right now we don't have hard evidence or the authority to search. Don't go looking for trouble.
(Staring hard at Tefi)
Sigh, didn't hear a word. More stubborn than a burdenbeast. At least wait until I'm gone before you make a move. Don't drag me into it.
Hold it, Nacho! Why are you at the observation hall again? I checked—you're not on the schedule today.
Aquila...
How many times have I told you? Even if you went a whole day without eating or drinking, soaking underwater hooking up power ports, even if you died on the job, the Iberians still wouldn't thank you.
I didn't become technical lead of the underwater work team to get them to thank me.
"I just don't want them to misunderstand the Islanders even more"... Yeah, yeah. Did you just go in the water again?
Mm... *hiss*.
The rust on your arm has spread all the way to the nerve interface in your shoulder, and—
What happened to the bolt in your joint? That was an old model Grandma Rufina left you. You can't find replacement parts for it anywhere!
Didn't I just get you waterproof coating and bio-barrier agent the day before yesterday? No, wait, the day before yesterday...
The day before yesterday, you went straight to the Islander Mutual Aid Society after your shift, Aquila.
Sorry. Come with me next time—you can remind me.
I'm not really comfortable with the atmosphere there.
What, it shatters your lovely dreams about Iberia?
Aquila, it's already good enough here.
It's not enough. Being able to choose your own work, not getting questioned by the Penal Battalion every day—Iberians think that's just normal life, but for us it's some kind of honor? Ridiculous!
And you know Grandma Rufina never wanted just this.
At least they've appointed an Ægir as the Salvage Center's new Supervisor.
It won't make a difference. A former Ægir Consul can't care about her kin in Iberia, and won't.
You're not going to her welcome party?
I'd rather go to the Mutual Aid Society and be with my real kin.
The ocean.
The mixed layer isn't very deep. The water here is always warm and bright. Tiny plankton drift about freely, like dust in the air.
The seabed.
The soil of the sea, and the place where Rea-Iberia sleeps.
It connects every island on the continental shelf, too. If you're interested, you could stroll along the seafloor and walk through every lost town.
*Huff*—*huff*—
Relax, Moreno. This diving suit is like having a finbeast's swim bladder. Don't be afraid of the current—let it lift you up.
I-I understand, Supervisor Clementia. I only meant to come to your welcome party, and now I'm walking underwater off Iberia's southern coast...
Think of it as my own special way of saying welcome.
Ægir and Iberia are both nations born of the sea. "Island," "wave," "seabed"... We share many words for the sea.
This flowing blue belt isn't frightening in itself. Perhaps one day you won't need an Ægir hologram—you'll be able to walk along the real seafloor, with no boundaries at all.
I can't believe it. I can feel the hazy sunlight on my face, the rough shell fragments under my feet, the current pushing at my back...
Ah, sorry, that's the Little Helper running the projection pushing you. I think it's trying to remind you that there are lots of other technicians waiting for their turn.
S-sorry.
Where is this? Such strange buildings, and so many Ægir in white robes... Are they swimming through the air?
My apologies, there's a small glitch in the environment simulation. Little Helper, recalibrate the data.
Supervisor Clementia, was that Ægir I just saw?
That was an Ægir underwater city, Milliarium—the place I once governed and lived in. My home.
Before I left, I took two days off: one to brush up on Iberian and service the language module in my body, and one to commit the city to memory.
What you saw was a scene recreated from my memories.
I don't even know if I should call it a city. It's so different from everywhere I've ever been... Ægir and us, we're just too far apart after all...
Supervisor Clementia, could you tell me how you say "Ægir" in Ægirian? I-I want to—
You want to know whether you have another name besides "Islander," don't you?
How did you know...
(In Ægirian) Ægir.
Please remember this: in the Ægirian lexicon, both you and I are called "Ægir."
Æ... gir...
(In halting Ægirian) "Ægir"...
Unrecognized word detected. User, please confirm with the speaker.
Clementia knew that the kin before her couldn't hear the language module's voice prompts. She was the only one who could see the warning pop-ups floating in the air.
Their forebears had left the ocean to live in Iberia. Perhaps by their parents' generation, the Ægirian language had already faded from memory.
Clementia's kind help opened parts of their minds they had never touched before.
"Sea," "swim," "Ægir," "the Ægir"...
Their halting Ægirian set Clementia's language module throwing errors again and again, until the pop-ups nearly blocked her view of her kin.
She had prepared herself before coming ashore. She knew that as the proposer of the Salvage Plan, as Ægir's representative, she could not interfere in Iberian policy.
Yet she still wanted to reach these kin who lived on land, to do something for them.

For now, at least, she didn't want to interrupt these kin who had been away from home for so very long. They had every right to reclaim the language of their homeland. But clearly, not all of them were willing to accept Clementia's goodwill.
All right, enough questions!
Ægirian's too distant from us. What use is learning it? To add one more suspicious charge to our list when the Inquisition interrogates us?
Sir, don't blame your friend. If you're unhappy, you can blame me directly.
Supervisor Clementia, I understand you don't mean any harm.
But in Iberia, especially for Islanders, getting close to the ocean is dangerous. The threats we face can't be wiped away with romantic, poetic words.
If we need help, we'll turn to kin who've suffered under Iberia the same as us. At least at the Mutual Aid Society, I don't have to doubt who I am.
Mutual Aid Society...
(In Ægirian) "Ægir."
Word recognized. Module calibrated. Clearing error prompts.
Hm?
If saying one proper word of Ægirian made someone more guilty, I'd have been sitting in a dungeon long ago.
Nacho?
Ægirian and Iberian sound very different, but once you find the knack, learning a word isn't too hard.
Whether it's "Islander" or "Ægir," they're both ways of naming us. Knowing one more means knowing a little more about "us," doesn't it?
Gaius, how about I take your underwater shift this afternoon? Ángela was already asking you to come home yesterday.
...She's not well. I'll go check on her.
Sorry, Supervisor Clementia.
They've just been carrying too much lately. Once they're actually using Ægir-made equipment and the underwater work gets easier, they won't be so aggressive.
Lightening their load is my job. Judging them isn't. Don't worry about it. And thank you for helping me out there, Nacho.
You're too kind.
You're on the underwater work team, aren't you? I heard that when the Inquisition first took over the Salvage Center, they lacked experience, and you helped them a great deal.
When you have time, introduce me to your friends. I understand Ægir's technology, and I'd like to understand the people who use it, too.
I'd be glad to.
Soledad, you made it. Last week you said you'd been having a lot of friction with the Iberians since you moved into the district. Have things gotten better?
Much better. I followed the advice of the Mentor and everyone here and kept evidence of my neighbors deliberately harming me.
Then I went to the Inquisitors and Penal Battalion soldiers at the checkpoint and told them my neighbors' behavior was affecting the progress of my salvage work.
I don't know if they did anything, but those neighbors did behave themselves a bit for a few days.
That's only a stopgap. If you need help, even after curfew, just light our signal, and kin will definitely come help you.
No... I mean, I'm very grateful, but I don't want to trouble you all anymore.
You're still worried we'll blow things up into a big deal, aren't you?
The Mentor told me this district is different from how things used to be back home. The Inquisition will treat us more fairly, and the Iberians won't hurt us on a whim.
That's why I came here. It really is a little better here than other places. That's enough.

I don't want to hurt you, but have you ever thought about this—if you couldn't operate Ægir technical equipment, if you were just an ordinary laborer handling logistics, would the Inquisition still help you?
After the Salvage Plan was announced, most of the Islanders they recruited were technical specialists in engineering or seafaring. It's not us they value—it's their own Salvage Plan.
After the Port City's Central District is salvaged, where do we go then? Get deported, or go back to the hometowns we hate? Not a single Iberian will remember what we gave.
That won't happen...
Won't happen? You've heard it yourself. When those Iberians proudly talk about the legends of the Port City their fathers told them, do they say even half a word about the Islanders?
They don't even know that the Port City's original design and construction were led by Islanders.
...If the Mentor were here today, he wouldn't agree with you.
Even without his agreement, we should do something for ourselves—even if it's only to "be remembered."
The smell of the sea...
Salvage ships—not contraband seized by the Inquisition, but vessels actually put into service. I always believed this day would come, and yet... it's hard to believe.
The shipyard paths are slippery. Please be careful, High Inquisitor Fidela.
You may have resigned as an Inquisitor, but as Dario's student, you're still one of the Inquisition's sharpest rapiers. So why, by my side, do you look like a cane propping up an old woman?
I meant no disrespect to you whatsoever!

It's only that ever since... my teacher fell, you've volunteered for nearly every Seaborn extermination operation. It was because of the lingering wounds from those battles that Su Santidad reassigned you to the shipyard.
Wounds eaten by the sea wind always heal a little slower. It's nothing serious.
As for Dario... When Su Santidad had me identify Dario's remains, all I saw was a handful of ash, burned from bones that might have been human or Seaborn.
But I know he died for Iberia's tomorrow. His name is carved somewhere the sea wind won't wear away anytime soon. That's enough.
Relax a little, Irene. Rea-Iberia is a different place. Here, we're about to witness Iberia shaking off its old affliction.
If that's how it goes—far from the dungeons, far from the old scores with the Islanders that can never be settled—what's so bad about keeping each other company at the shipyard?
You're right.

It's just that I thought Su Santidad would assign you to a patrol unit. Putting a High Inquisitor who once stood against storms and abominations in charge of a shipyard that salvages wreckage is rather...
Salvaging wreckage and mending ships certainly aren't a High Inquisitor's duties.
But before we used them to burn the Seaborn, lanterns were first and foremost tools to light the way through sea fog.
If the Port City is to become a port linking land and sea, then Iberians need to relearn how to build ships and go to sea.
That's almost exactly what Lord Carmen said.
I am his student, after all. In all these years, he's taught me more than just how to kill Seaborn.
But there are some things I could never learn, no matter how long I stayed by his side...
High Inquisitor Fidela?
It's nothing.
A ship that's sailed too long through the fog needs to catch its breath now and then. As it happens, this is the place to mend it.
I'll follow Su Santidad's wishes and rest up properly here.
This is the underwater observation hall. It's used to operate the cranes that hold up the Outer District and the Central District.
The technicians' job is to connect the power lines between the lighthouses and the cranes, so the thirty-seven lighthouses can power the cranes for the rest of the Salvage Plan.
Supervisor Clementia, you've been staring out the window this whole time. Are you worried about the underwater work?
Hmm... The ones working right now are the technicians from Team Two, right? The brown-haired one is Soledad, and the quickest one is Matthew.
Looks like you already know the salvage team well enough without me introducing them.
I've only memorized a few names. That hardly counts as knowing them.
When I served in the Exercitus, the way I remembered every soldier's name was to pair each person with a coordinate on a sea route. Every combination of numbers is unique, and so is every person.
That method sounds even more complicated...

Remembering and knowing are entirely different things. I believe that only after real conversation does cold information turn into a feeling that lets you know a person, or a land.
But until I find the right opportunity, all that information and knowledge can only be stored away in my head for now. For example—
Rufina.
She was your grandmother, wasn't she? She helped build the Port City and was an outstanding worker. I'm sorry for your loss.
You really remember... There's no need to apologize. It's been ten years since Grandma passed away from her illness. I've gotten used to living on my own.
She made my prosthetic. It makes me feel like Grandma's always with me, but now...
Hm? What's that bumping into my leg?
Malfunction detected, malfunction detected.
Limb module severely worn. For a better tomorrow for us all, users must strictly observe the eight-hour workday.
—Patient pain level detected nearing tolerance threshold. Limb module must be removed immediately. Preparing for surgery.
W-wait—
Settle down, Little Helper.
Huh... You... You pulled its rotary blade off with your bare hands?

This Little Helper is fitted with a wartime medical module. Physically interrupting it is faster than a voice command. Sorry—I scanned your vital signs and the condition of your prosthetic without asking.
I think the little robot threw an error because I lost a bolt from my prosthetic during underwater work a few days ago.
Would you let me take a look? I'll be a bit more polite than the Little Helper.
All right.
Remarkable. Every part used in this prosthetic is as ordinary as can be, but its ingenious structure seems to suit your needs perfectly.
Still, the corrosion is far too severe, and the wound at the connection is worse than I imagined. There are burn scars, too. Have you been working through the pain this whole time?
Because pain can be endured. As for the burns... They came from a firebomb thrown into my room over ten years ago. I got out alive, but I couldn't save my arm.
A terrible accident.
Yeah. That was the first time I ever saw Grandma look so heartbroken.
She was a tough, strict elder. Even when kids my age went off early to reclaim salt flats or catch fin, she was still set on making me study Ægirian and engineering design.
No wonder your Ægirian is so precise.
If she knew I'd deliberately ignored her warnings, gone in the water with my prosthetic, and lost her part on top of that, I don't know how angry she'd be...
A single bolt that fell into the vast sea... I doubt I'll ever find it.
Even a single bolt makes ripples when it falls into the sea. It may not be lost for good.
But the urgent matter is your prosthetic. You want to keep doing underwater work and salvage the Port City's Central District with your own hands?
Yes. It's important to me.
All right. I can have the Little Helper print you a prosthetic better suited to your work right now. The design will take some time, but at least you won't be distracted by pain while you work.
Thank you, Supervisor Clementia.
What's going on?
Someone in a Penal Battalion uniform is wandering around the Salvage Center.
Investigating a case?
Doesn't look like it. She seems to be checking something in the sign-in logs with Aquila.
Picking on us on purpose again? I thought at least here we wouldn't have to deal with that.
Hard to say. But that Penal Battalion soldier seems to be an Islander too.
Aquila...?
Officer, wasn't this a routine ID check? Isn't it over yet?

Oh dear, so sorry. Ms. Aquila, right? Just confirm the entry and exit records here...
Ah!
Hold the pen steady.
Thanks, kind kin.
I've never heard of Islanders in the Penal Battalion.
Strictly speaking, I don't really count as Inquisition. I'm just a nobody without even a unit number.
They ought to value us.
If they valued me any more, they'd give me more work. Training recruits is already miserable enough.
You're a Penal Battalion instructor...

You're right to be nervous. Just now, when you bent down to pick up the pen, I confirmed that one of the air tank hoses on your back is missing—and I happened to pick up a similar one on a stretch of coast far from the observation hall.
On the day of the launch ceremony, you should've finished your shift's tasks early, but your gear turned up outside the work zone. Care to explain where you went?
I—
She went to get medicine for me.
Nacho? Supervisor Clementia?
O-officer, you can see this hand of mine. That day was when my prosthetic was due for maintenance.

Aquila looks out for every one of our kin. She always goes out of her way to buy me waterproof coating and bio-barrier agent, and she's never missed once. Sh-she might still have the receipt from that day.
Oh my, looks like I misunderstood. But—
My apologies, ma'am. I've checked the records over and over, and I can't find any notice of an Inquisition investigation.
You must be Supervisor Clementia? Don't take it the wrong way—this isn't an investigation. I didn't mean to disturb your great salvage work, but this uniform does stick out like a sore thumb.
The Penal Battalion is usually stationed at the checkpoints outside the Salvage Center, recording the technicians' comings and goings. Eyes that see everything surely needn't doubt what they've seen.
Of course. This is just a spur-of-the-moment visit. I've never seen kin from the deep sea with my own eyes before.
I'd say we both have pointed ears.
Haha, of course. In Milliarium, you must have been a very popular Consul...
Too bad this is Iberia.
I'll take my leave.
Aquila.
Supervisor Clementia, I know nothing about anything that Penal Battalion soldier accused me of.
You don't need to explain yourself to me, Aquila. That soldier was right about one thing—this is Iberia. If I can't verify her judgment myself, I won't say anything more for now.
In my two days at the Salvage Center, I've talked with the technicians. Most of them trust you a great deal.
I've only done what I should. I'll solve the problems they have to face as Islanders.
By what means?
By any means.
I thought you'd just tell me you'd joined a Mutual Aid Society.
Someone told you... But helping our kin doesn't break any Inquisition commandments.
Of course. I just want to know if I can join.
You've run into trouble too?
I want to solve your troubles.
...The Mentor said we're a Mutual Aid Society for all Ægir. Its doors are open to every Ægir who's confused, suffering, or longing for peace.
But I think that apart from appearances, Supervisor Clementia has nothing in common with us—with the Islanders. I'm afraid you wouldn't be welcome.
I see.
If you want to ask, then ask.
Afraid you'll hear the answer you fear most? Then you shouldn't have lied for me just now.
Aquila, you saw it too—Supervisor Clementia obviously noticed something, but she still spoke up for you.
As long as the Port City's Central District is salvaged successfully, our lives will get better. You—
You've always been like this. Always thinking that as long as you do well enough, recite scripture diligently enough, you can wipe away prejudice.
When you got dragged into what happened with Grandma Rufina, you said nothing. And now, even though you obviously don't want me going back to the Mutual Aid Society, you still won't say a word.
Aquila...
But you did cover for me in front of the Penal Battalion and Supervisor Clementia just now. For you, that wasn't easy.
Nacho, whether or not you agree with how I think, as a friend, there's just one thing I'm asking of you.
If anything happens to me in the next few days, you can go to the church where the Mutual Aid Society meets and find our Mentor. He'll help me.
Until then, do what you do best. Don't ask anything, and don't say anything.
I never pry into what you do, Aquila. I just don't want someone else I know to end up in danger.
Like my grandmother, Rufina.
Thank you... thank you... Mentor, I know what to do now.
Go on, kin.
Let go of your hatred, and you will find true peace within. If the waters stir again, I will still be here to listen.
Forgive me, kin. There are so many lost souls. I want to help them as best I can, but my abilities are limited.
But by now, you should understand why peace is precious, and why strife is foolish.
It's true it's not very convenient for you to move about the church like this. I'll drop the disguise... Where were we with our experiment?
Hmm, my kin, there's no need to be curious about these alchemical instruments. They're only afterimages of another experiment—my memories.
Return to We Many? No, you need to keep me company a while longer.
Nurturing offspring, relaying information, assimilating the other... None of that is your duty anymore. The experiment is going well. You've proven you can suppress your instincts.
Next, all I need to do is replace the fin in the tank with—
Sorry to disturb you, Bishop Aulus...
No disturbance at all. I'm glad to share my experiment with you. It's one part of the future we envision together.
And please, forget that title of "Bishop" for now.
We are fellow travelers, neither high nor low. It's only that, at present, I understand and command a little more knowledge than you, so for the moment I play a more important role.
You've come from the Salvage Center... My arrangements didn't work?
No, just as you predicted, our kin did run into trouble, but the problem was resolved before we could step in.
A young Ægir covered for her. He knows nothing about our plan.
Oh?
Kin, tell me—what sort of person is he?
Perhaps I should thank you.
For what?
For asking my opinion before connecting the hologram, and for not being so fond of that tedious "tactile simulation module."
I'm not Horatia, after all. If I wanted to hug you, I'd do it in person.
Please don't.
How are the Hunters?

Laurentina reaches toward the scent of blood even in her dreams, and Skadi's attitude toward slaughtering Seaborn could be called "enthusiastic." I can't tell whether that's Mártus's influence or the Doctor's.
Is that a good thing or a bad thing?
I can't judge. Just as I can't judge whether Ulpianus's strange behavior is proof that some of his reason remains, or a sign that he's fallen completely.
Everything we know of him comes from the Seaborn that still try to talk to the Hunters. They describe Ulpianus's movements the way one would describe a companion's.
He still intends to go to the Caerula Arbor?
I'll greet him with my lance... whether or not he brings back an answer.
You're not much more clearheaded than he is, Clementia.
Hm?

Months ago, you were supposed to be Kal'tsit and the Doctor's guide in the home territories. Instead, at the last minute, you proposed a follow-up plan for cooperation with Iberia to the Institute of Scientific Development Planning.
Salvaging Rea-Iberia. The first time I heard it, I thought you'd gone mad.
Horatia thought so too.

Once the waterway opened, I was supposed to accompany the Doctor and Dr. Kal'tsit to the home territories. But Horatia quickly issued an assessment report on behalf of the Institute stating that I was "unsuitable" for the assignment.
She found out what you've been hiding? Or might their trip uncover an even bigger secret, one you're not permitted to know?
Either is possible. In the end, I could only stay on the shore and keep working as head of the Waterway Program.
Fortunately, the Doctor, Dr. Kal'tsit, and I had already reached an understanding on certain issues beforehand. Salvaging the Port City and rebuilding Iberia's harbor was a decision we made together.
—But not a plan Ægir would like. Clearly, you're not too fond of it either.
Still, before I left, Horatia seemed to understand that even people on land deserve at least a little respect—and approving the Salvage Plan was her "respect."
It's just that once the Salvage Plan is over—whether it succeeds or not—the Institute of Scientific Development Planning will reassess the next steps for Iberia's development.
—As if "Iberia" were just a coordinate on a map, rather than someone's home.
Knowing your talent for asking for trouble, I take it you don't want any of that to happen.
That's right, but not out of some kind of... pity.
In the common understanding of the Ægir, Iberia undoubtedly suffered a devastating blow after the Profound Silence.
In the war against the Seaborn, it may still be struggling, but in truth, it has already lost.
The Hunters have worked with the Inquisition many times. Their soldiers have more than enough strength of will, but their methods of war are still too simple.
A nation that has already "lost" its war for survival like this belongs to the past in Ægir's textbooks...
But I believe we can find the future here.
You mean Rea-Iberia, which is about to return?
Not entirely.
I believe that in Iberia, in the Iberians themselves, I can find a way to face... a future that isn't so bright.
I don't understand what you mean.
All I know is that for the sake of these ideas I don't understand, you made a bet with Horatia.
Yes. Before she uses her "efficient" methods to turn Iberia into an Ægir on land, I need to prove to her that Iberia deserves to exist—and must exist—in its own way.
But if you fail this time, the price will be losing both your titles of Consul and Honorary Exercitus Commander for good.
Putting myself on the table is a much better deal than having to use the Abyssal Hunters and Rhodes Island as chips. When it comes to you all, I'm a miser.
...Our partnership still stands. The Abyssal Hunters will be on your side.
At least until you lose the bet.
Cold, but reassuring. Thank you, Gladiia.
I can hear you writing. You can just come in, Tacita.
Your communications with Abyssal Hunters Captain Gladiia are classified. I shouldn't know about them, nor interrupt them.
And yet the moment you knew who I was talking to, a guess had already formed in your mind. Most of the time, it's guesses that move people to act.
Please, come here, Tacita, Consul's Aide of the Institute of Scientific Development Planning.
I know you and Ms. Horatia disagree politically, so I don't understand. When she insisted you bring a member of the Institute ashore with you, why did you choose me?
Was it to put Ms. Horatia at ease? Because you knew I voted against your proposal? Or because you wanted to deliberately make things hard for an inexperienced newcomer? Or perhaps—
Tacita stepped forward as she spoke, yet her barrage of questions did not shake Clementia's smile in the slightest.
Suddenly, she broke off.
The former Consul under her verbal "assault" bent down without a care and began fixing the ribbon on her suitcase. Only then did Tacita notice that the knot she had tied earlier had come undone.
The reason I chose you is simple. The ribbon on your case had come untied at the time, and I remembered my Little Helper had stored a lovely knotting technique modeled on the tail of a ribbonfin.
I knew nothing at all about the dozens of members Horatia brought. You were the only one who made me realize there was something I could do for you.
...Just because of that?
Mm. Besides, I can tell you care deeply about Ægir. That's reason enough for me to trust you.
Any other questions? We've already reached an agreement with the Inquisition, but construction will still run into plenty of trouble, and I need to deal with it quickly.
The technicians' shifts don't rotate often enough. We can't push the work forward at the cost of their health.
Aquila's situation needs following up. Until we have the results of an investigation, it could well do more harm than good if the Inquisition got involved.
Ah, and Nacho. His prosthetic needs attention, and that lost bolt...
Ms. Clementia.
Hm?
I greatly respect how meticulous you are in your work, and your passion for the Salvage Plan.
But I must say, I've reread your proposal six times, and I still believe that cooperating with Iberia as equals carries great risk, and does nothing for Ægir's development.
I understand your concerns, Tacita.
I'll be careful. And I have to succeed.
Ridiculous!

The Salvage Center is Supervisor Clementia's responsibility, and we're at a crucial stage of our cooperation with Ægir. Under no circumstances should you barge straight into the Salvage Center and interrogate whatever suspect you can grab.
I—
Enough. Just do your job in the patrol unit and stay out of any investigations into the Islanders.
...Yes, sir.
Hm? What's this thing?
An Ægir general-purpose assistance machine. You see them all over the Salvage Center. Instructor Drusa was in such a hurry to crack the case earlier, she may not have noticed.
Sorry, sorry. You heard it just now—I promise I won't bother you all at work again.
You'll be back.
...This robot can detect lies?
Guessing what's in someone's heart doesn't take sophisticated technology. It just takes nerve.
Haha, now you're the one fishing for answers. Back at the Salvage Center, I took you for a good boss, upright to the point of being stiff.
All right, I really can't promise I'll stop. But you don't need to worry. My wanting to investigate has nothing to do with my position as a Penal Battalion instructor.
I'm an Islander too. I know how much resentment my kin hold toward the Inquisition, toward Iberia. Sometimes I even turn a blind eye.
Unfortunately, a vague theory has already taken shape in my head, and now that I've found a few clues, I can't let it go.
I don't want to work against you, Supervisor Clementia, but you can't stamp out a person's curiosity.
Your "curiosity" is exactly what I want.
Wait, you're not here to stop me—you're here to work with me?
You said it yourself: this is Iberia. I need to solve problems the Iberian way.
I understand. Because the Salvage Plan needs so many technicians, the Inquisition has called back a lot of capable Islanders, and it's shouldering considerable risk.
For me, and for Lord Iberia, the Salvage Plan must succeed. A large-scale search right now would only throw everyone into a panic, but that doesn't mean we can only react as things come.
So you came to me... What's my pay?
A lead—Aquila has joined an Islander Mutual Aid Society.
That's a convenient cover... That's the only lead?
It should be enough for you. When you went straight to Aquila, you weren't trying to follow a lead in the first place. You wanted to put pressure on them so they'd rush into acting.
Tch, you've said it all. I'll get to the bottom of it as soon as I can. If Aquila really is planning something, she might make her move soon.
Until the investigation turns something up, I can't give you any support openly. But if you need it, I can lend you the Little Helper.
Little Helper is wholeheartedly at your service, for a better tomorrow for us all—
How do you turn this thing off...
You'll get along just fine.
Still not talking?
N-nothing to say. Sabotaging the launch ceremony was planned by the three of us alone. You want me to give up accomplices? You're wasting your time.
Wasting my time? I'm just using the wrong interrogation method.
You there, recruit. Stop staring at the wall and hand me the rapier.
R-rapier? Don't tell me you mean to...
No, we can't interrogate a suspect like that. Under the Port City Outer District's new rules, we're not even supposed to carry weapons in the dungeon.
Spare me. Did you join the Inquisition to give humanitarian care to criminals?
I joined the Inquisition to protect my family, so they can see Iberia's tomorrow, sir.
Good. Has your family moved to the Outer District, soldier?
They all have. They want to see Rea-Iberia's Central District rise, too. My father used to secretly tell me all kinds of stories about the Port City—
Ah, not for any sinister purpose, of course. Just bedtime stories to get a kid to sleep.
What if it were your family crushed under a building they blew up? What if it were your home those disgusting Sea Terrors took over when they came ashore?
That's...
We have no way of knowing how many atrocities these vicious heretics committed before this plot. Even for the sake of the Iberian families they've hurt, you still can't bring yourself to do it?

The young Penal Battalion soldier looked at the weapons at his waist. At the training grounds, he had imagined lighting people's way with the lantern in his hand, cutting down Seaborn with his rapier, blasting the waves with his handcannon.
But he had never imagined that the lanterns kindled by willpower would hang swaying on dungeon walls, casting his own twisted shadow.
It was not only Sea Terror slime that rusted a rapier, but also blood spilled in interrogations—and his handcannon had never yet been fired.
I—
Lower the rapier, soldier.
Your Excellency the High Inquisitor!
I told you, you came here to get away from war—whether it's against the Seaborn or the Islanders.
High Inquisitor Fidela, before you left to take up your post at the shipyard, you said you'd interrogate these Church of the Deep cultists yourself. I shouldn't have acted on my own.
But I've always followed your command. I know you haven't had a decent night's sleep since High Inquisitor Dario fell. It's rare that you've finally been sent to rest at the shipyard...
And in all the long time I've followed you, you've never let us take part in interrogating Islanders. Can we really not earn your trust?
No. I'd trust any one of you to watch my back on the battlefield. The Seaborn are our common enemy.
But these Church of the Deep cultists who've strayed from the path are not the same as the Islanders.

I haven't reported to Su Santidad that I'm still conducting interrogations. Call it my own inability to let go. I don't want you all still studying the rules of surviving in the dark on the eve of dawn.
Young soldier, you should never have to draw your weapon when you don't want to hurt anyone. I believe Iberia's tomorrow will be like that.
Please leave this to me. I'll interrogate this cultist in a dignified manner.
I'm sorry, sir. I can't be that mature yet... but thank you.
Heh... heh heh... What a moving speech, Your Excellency the High Inquisitor.

"Iberia's tomorrow"... It's precisely because you're always going on about it that it'll never come...
Since the High Inquisitor is so merciful, would you be willing to take these chains off my hands? After all, Rea-Iberia's a place full of hope, where there shouldn't be any bloody war, isn't it—
Aagh!
The cultist's consciousness was severed—and so were his chained hands.
Mm, blood. Looks like you haven't yet been taken into the "embrace of the sea" you dream of day and night. I've "taken off" your chains for you. No need to thank me.
Your kind is always long-tongued, sinister, and full of lies. But you're also cowards.
If you were willing to risk arrest by showing up at the launch ceremony, that means you'd already prepared yourselves to be sacrificed.
(Groans in agony)
I've brought plenty of potent hemostatic medicine. And it's not for my own use.
The night is long. You can start from your hometown, or from the parents who abandoned you, and I'll listen. But in the end, you must give me an answer, all right?
Who exactly are your accomplices?
The sun has yet to leap from the sea, and the lost are still dreaming.
Can't sleep? Has returning home stirred you so?
You know better than anyone that I no longer need sleep.
But you still dream, and so do I. That's why we were able to work together.
This church is almost exactly like the one where we first met.
I know your aims, and I know what kind of man you are. You can drop the illusions.
If a few small tricks can help us fulfill our long-held wishes sooner, why not?
The plan hasn't changed?
That's right.
However, my kin have recently made up their minds. They may need some help.
What you want me to do, I'll do. After that, we owe each other nothing, and we're done with each other.
Owe each other nothing... I told you, I never needed him to repay anything.
Heavens, aren't you the girl who was butting heads with the Inquisition in the square? What're you doing at the shipyard gate? Ea, Colón de, Todo... what was it again?
It's Estefanía Colón de Toledo!
I've seen you everywhere these past few days, preaching stories about the Golden Age. Are you really a descendant of the Royal Navy?
Would I lie—
All of Iberia's nobles, and our Golden Age, are dead. Every priest and every book of scripture says so.
Salvador...
If you think they're dead, then why are you standing here, taking part in the salvage?
"Saints above, I shall follow the guidance of the embodiment of Iberia's virtue."
"I pray that ye wield the light of judgment to cleanse our sinful bodies, and drive out the abominations born of sin."
I should be ashamed for consorting with the likes of you, an embodiment of sin. Where's my salt... I must keep watch over myself...
So you've got no hopes at all for our glorious past, not even for what Rea-Iberia looks like?
How pitiful. How many times did the priest back home make you copy out scripture? The Inquisition's scriptures were always—
You can chat with them later. Inquisition investigation. Please come with me.
You again? You stopped me on the day of the launch ceremony, and now you're after me again today!

Spouting lies, stirring up the crowd... I suspect you're up to something. But this is the Port City's Outer District, so I won't arrest you outright. I only ask that you cooperate with an identity check.
Officer, please wait...
I think you can see that she only pretends to be a noble to make money, and those Golden Age stories are just exaggerations to draw attention...
If she's only out for money, as you say, and hasn't colluded with heretics, she'll be released once questioning is over.
Please understand. It's all for Iberia's purity and virtue.
But the way you uphold them isn't what the Inquisition expects, Nando García Rubio.
High Inquisitor Fidela?
Why are you making trouble at the shipyard gate? Who's your instructor? Do I need to repeat what the patrol unit's job is?
It has nothing to do with Instructor Drusa. I noticed something off myself and wanted to look into it further.
Where's your investigation warrant?
I don't have one...
You can't even invent a pretext. Should I call that honest, or dim?
Head up, soldier. Return to your post. I won't tie your hands, but before you act next time, you'd better think hard about why you're acting at all.
Yes...
Thank you for that, Your Excellency the High Inquisitor.
I didn't defend you.
She's still a swindler, and the two of you preaching openly at the shipyard gate has disrupted order here.
Why are you still here instead of taking her home?
That's exactly what I wanted to ask for your help with...
The Inquisition actually let you go?
Phew— I-I told you all, I'm a descendant of the Royal Navy. As long as you become my supporters, I can shelter you too.
Support... how do we support you?
My heart is set on rebuilding the Royal Navy fleet, and I'm still on that long journey. It's just that putting a fleet together takes funding...
A hundred years ago, sure, the common folk had to pay taxes to the nobles, but we don't have that kind of money now...
It doesn't have to be money! Even a meal or a place to stay would do.
Once Rea-Iberia is salvaged and our fleet officially sets sail from the harbor, maybe we can even swindle... *ahem*, earn even more wealth!
I've known her for a few months. She's always lived by conning people and telling stories. I was badly injured and can't work. Without her help, I'd probably have starved to death long ago.
Even so, I can't just watch a young person keep making mistakes.
She has an excellent memory, she loves dealing with people, and she's traveled so far that she practically has a map of Iberia drawn in her head.
A map?
Yes. And not just a map of Iberia as it is now.
She talks to displaced people and remembers their stories, and where their hometowns stood before the sea swallowed them.
What she remembers holds what Iberia should have looked like.
Once Rea-Iberia's Central District rises, we may need to salvage more sunken towns. If so...
She'd be well suited to working at the shipyard.
Her family abandoned her very young, and for certain reasons she can't do manual labor.
If Iberia's future is as bright as the Central District that's about to rise, then perhaps she won't have to live by swindling anymore...
You want her to live with more dignity?
Iberians ought to possess lofty virtue. You believe that too, don't you?
...I understand.
You may have genuinely interfered with Inquisition business, but this district will give you one more chance.
Have her report to the shipyard. We can use her.
Outside the shipyard, the crowd kept growing. At first, people had only been drawn by the quarrel and the Liberi's ringing voice, and wanted to see what was going on—
They never expected to become captivated by the stories a young girl told.
You over there, the sailmaker. You said you're from Goldwave, on Goldwave Bay?

A filthy little town smothered in thick fog all year round. The priest there said the town's name was the source of its sins. Poor catches, crops that won't grow—all the name's fault. Now it's been renamed Waveless.
What a shame. In my ancestors' telling, the buildings there were all white, because they needed no dye—the setting sun gilded them on its own. And the townsfolk were all expert fin-fishers.
But it wasn't because they knew so much about the habits of the schools of fin. It was because they fished farther afield than any other town.

Every time they went fishing, their boats went far from shore, but they weren't afraid. They knew that as long as they looked back before nightfall, the golden glow of the buildings would always guide them home.
There's a story like that...?

Of course! And Goldwave produced many talented people who were given titles and offices for their mastery of seafaring and sailmaking. They say their descendants still live in the town, just unaware of who their ancestors were...
I am better with a needle than my neighbors... Could it be...
What luck! Lady de Toledo happens to be assembling a naval fleet, and a sailmaker is exactly what I'm missing. Isn't that a coincidence? Maybe our ancestors even met in the Royal Navy fleet!
Yes, yes!
(Mouthing) Valerio! Valerio, look! I found another supporter! Tonight's dinner is taken care of!
Why's there such a crowd on this street today? Good. It'll give our operation cover.
Aquila, you're late. Did you have work this morning? You look like you just came out of the water.
It's nothing. I went to take care of some personal business.
Was the item delivered? It's important for the operation in a few days.
Don't worry. The Penal Battalion can't keep eyes on everything.
Take another route.
The old pipeline they used to transport live fin? Only our kin know about that one.
Go.
...Damn.
A route only Islanders know isn't necessarily safe, you know. After all, not every Islander is a dangerous element, right?
*Hiss*...
You again!
I really was a fool to think of you as kin.
Didn't you let down your kin's goodwill too? That boy Nacho—he's terrible at lying, and you never thought twice about dragging him in.
Behave. What are you trying to do?
Take this to Nacho.
A bolt?
His hand can't wait any longer. Hmph. Working for the Iberians, wearing himself down to this state.
Instructor Drusa, I believe I warned you not to act on your own again.
Operations unit? That was fast... You've had your eye on Aquila too?
No comment. We'll be handling the questioning from here. Please return to your patrol unit duties.
Cuff her and take her away.
*Pant*... *pant*...
Why... Aquila still...
You're Nacho, the technician?
Ms. Tacita, is Supervisor Clementia here?! I need to see her urgently—Aquila's been taken by the Inquisition!
Aquila's been arrested? Supervisor Clementia isn't here right now. Just... don't panic. I'll contact her as soon as I can.
Also, your arm looks like it's in terrible shape. Should I treat it first?
Nacho?
She's not here?
Nacho, whether or not you agree with how I think, as a friend, there's just one thing I'm asking of you.
If anything happens to me in the next few days, you can go to the church where the Mutual Aid Society meets and find our Mentor. He'll help me.
Until then, do what you do best. Don't ask anything, and don't say anything.
Mutual Aid Society...
Hey, don't go!
Aquila's been arrested?
She used the commotion at the shipyard to make a deal in the crowd. I used a little trick to lure her and her accomplice somewhere convenient to make the grab.
Unfortunately, she'd already finished the exchange. She's being interrogated now, and I doubt I can get involved.
Aquila's resolve is strong. I'm worried a heavy-handed interrogation will backfire.
That deal was obviously preparation for something later, but so far she hasn't given up any information.
I'll keep following the Mutual Aid Society lead. Hopefully I can find some leads before this unknown threat hits.
But I have to warn you, Aquila isn't the only Islander caught up in this.
Even if the Inquisition wants to keep things stable, it can't ignore a danger sitting right out in the open.
I'll find a way to handle this.
As I said before, a large-scale search would get in the way of the Salvage Plan. More importantly, it would stir up Iberian resentment toward the Islanders all over again.
Reconciling the Islanders and the Iberians is a wish Lord Iberia and I share. When Islanders harm Iberia's interests, they're really harming themselves.
If we can't break this vicious cycle, then even if Rea-Iberia returns to the coastline, it won't bring the Iberian people together.
Sigh, Su Santidad sure handed you a tough job.
I've never been able to ignore anyone who asks for help.
You can call me arrogant.
I don't insult people who go looking for trouble.
Oh, right. When Aquila was arrested, she asked me to pass something along. The Inquisition inspected it and found nothing dangerous, so I brought it.
The bolt Nacho lost... She found it in the sea?
It's different from all the other parts in his prosthetic. It looks like a relic from the Golden Age. No wonder Nacho was so attached to it...
Aquila really does care about her kin. Someone with that much grit—why go down the wrong path? The bad blood between the Islanders and Iberia really grinds people down.
Your Excellency the High Inquisitor, the prisoner is here.
Is there anything else you need from us?
Go stand guard at the shipyard. And take a message to Irene. Tell her... my injuries have worsened again and I'm unwell. If Su Santidad has business to discuss today, ask her to go in my place.
Yes, sir.
So Inquisitors lie to their own colleagues too. That actually makes me feel a little better—so it's not only about the Islanders that you make up stories.
Don't bother provoking me.
I've dealt with far too many cultists and ordinary Islanders. The innocent, the hateful, the deranged... I've seen nearly everything. So I know how to handle your kind.
You could say I understand you better than you understand yourselves.
How dare you...!
I don't mean to insult you. But it's the only way I can avoid making mistakes.
I bear no hatred toward Islanders. Letting innocent people die for nothing would only taint my devotion to Iberia's noble virtue.
At the shipyard, I've slowly come to understand something—some ships can't sail the sea even after they've been repaired.

The Inquisition noticed the Mutual Aid Society's movements long ago. It's just that your gatherings have been so well hidden that I've begun to suspect someone is using some unusual Arts to cover for you.
Today we can finally have a proper talk. Tell me, what exactly are you all trying to do?
The Mutual Aid Society's church... The block Aquila told me about should be this one. Where is it...
Ngh...
Confusion, panic, sorrow, and rage were trapped inside Nacho's body, making him overlook how much worse the wound on his arm had become.
He wanted to know why Aquila would rather risk her life than live a peaceful, stable life. He wanted strife to vanish from Iberia. He wanted to find a solution to every problem.
A door opened for Ægir who were confused, suffering, and longing for peace.
(Semiconscious) Church...
At last we meet, Nacho. Don't worry. I'm Aquila's Mentor. I'll help you.
You're finally back. The technician Aquila—
I already know.
You know? Did you run into Nacho?
Nacho?
He wanted your help after what happened to Aquila, but when he saw you weren't here, he left.
Send the Little Helper to look for him. We can't afford any more accidents among the Salvage Center's people.
Has the Inquisition taken more people?
Not yet, but see for yourself.
Aquila, Soledad, Matthew, Gaius... The investigation list the Inquisition sent covers a third of the Salvage Center's staff, and every one of them is Ægir.
Aquila's case has already dragged in many Islanders. You understand that handling their problem carries diplomatic risk.
Even though you and I can both guess that the Inquisition actually needs this diplomatic cooperation to resolve its conflict with the Islanders?
I don't believe people on land are rational enough to face this situation head-on without interpreting Ægir's actions as "meddling in their family affairs."
Then what do you think about the Islanders themselves?
Forgive me for being blunt. Ægir accepted the choice of those of our kin who chose to go to land, but it also reached a consensus—they would have to bear the consequences of their choice.
And now their descendants have lived in Iberia for a long time. They're used to the Iberian way of doing things and know nothing whatsoever of Ægir's systems and ideals.
That being so, why should we forcibly intervene as kin in their conflict with Iberia?
It would only make it look as though all of Ægir's past tolerance existed simply because we had never seen with our own eyes what these Islanders truly went through.
You think I sympathize too much with what the Islanders have been through, and that sympathy is out of place. Is that it?
Yes.
Why did the first Ægir to leave the home territories come ashore?
The Seaborn overran their homes. They were... refugees.
Ægir cannot deny that it failed to protect its own people, let alone do what the Institute of Scientific Development Planning boasts of—"giving every citizen a choice."
That's exactly why I can't stand by and ignore their plight under the banner of "respect."
We see many things about Ægir very differently, Tacita. I won't ask you to agree with me. In fact, I don't think you should simply agree with the views Ægir hands you, either.
Whenever you have doubts, whenever you have conjectures, you're free to dispel them, to test them. I'll support you.
But sympathy is never out of place. Even from a purely rational standpoint, sympathy offers a whole new way of thinking—one that keeps people from finding the wrong answer out of pride.
I understand... No, I'll think about it some more.
Mm. Go on.
I hope you've been well, Lord Iberia.
At the salvage launch ceremony, you tacitly agreed that Ægir, represented by me, has the right to take part in handling the Islander question.
Yes, I've made my decision.
Diplomatic language is bound to be twisted by someone, and personally I'd rather face problems head-on than avoid them...
But I hope the Islanders who are already worn out from all this strife can have a chance to choose—
To choose whether to stay in Iberia, or return to Ægir.
Su Santidad.
Where is High Inquisitor Fidela?
Her Excellency's injuries have worsened again. She's taken leave from the shipyard and asked me to come in her place.
Fidela, my student... Even with a promise of the future set before her, she still doubts. But perhaps that is for the best.
You mean Her Excellency doesn't actually want to come to the Port City's Outer District?
No. She believes in Iberia's tomorrow, yet fears it will betray her. She will not accept my counsel, nor will she listen to more complicated explanations.
Su Santidad, High Inquisitor Fidela is exhausted. If her resolve has wavered, I... I'm sorry, but I think it would be completely understandable.
Her resolve has never wavered, Irene.
That is precisely why she did not come today.
Then I...
Do you know who I was speaking with just now?
It must have been Supervisor Clementia, presumably about the technician Aquila's arrest.
What do you make of her actions?
In Milliarium, I once asked the Ægir what they thought of the Islander question.
They expressed understanding in a very rational way. It could hardly even be called "sympathy"—it was a different kind of "indifference."
So I believe that Supervisor Clementia's intervention in Iberia's Islander question is most likely her own personal decision.
Do you believe such a personal decision goes against the will of Ægir?
If her will can lead Ægir toward a farther future, then her will may become Ægir's will as well.
Light your lantern, Irene.
Yes.
Su Santidad, which way are we going?
Down.
I came here on the day I became an Inquisitor. I still remember the Seaborn imprisoned inside.
Every Inquisitor must face it once before becoming an Inquisitor.
